walkthroughs.body_html:
Theory & Methods — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theory & Methods brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theory & Methods.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Weber's concept for empathetic understanding of social action is:
options: Anomie
Verstehen
Praxis
Alienation

mcqs.q: Which research method involves in-depth participant observation?
options: Survey
Experiment
Ethnography
Content analysis

mcqs.q: How does labelling theory explain ethnic differences in achievement?
options: Teacher stereotypes lead to differential expectations and self-fulfilling prophecies.
Marx defined class by occupational status like the Registrar General.
Schools have no influence on outcomes.
Different ethnic groups have different innate abilities.

mcqs.q: How did Marx define social class?
options: Ethnocentrism means concentrating on your own ethnic group only.
Marx defined class by how much money people earn.
Marx defined class by occupational status like the Registrar General.
By relationship to the means of production: the bourgeoisie own productive resources; the proletariat sell their labour. Class is a structural relationship, not just income level.

Judging other cultures by the standards of one's own — assuming one's own cultural practices and values are normal or superior. It is a methodological problem in social research as well as a social phenomenon.
Ethnocentrism is the same as racism.
Marx defined class by occupational status like the Registrar General.
Ethnocentrism means concentrating on your own ethnic group only.
